pages.title: Retained 55-item form
pages.description: Teacher self-reflection using the author’s English translations from Table S1. Choose the frequency that describes your practice. There are no teacher grades or performance rankings. You may leave items blank when you cannot describe them. No fixed recall window was specified in the published item table. This unscored form does not reproduce the paper’s ESEM factor scores. Do not enter pupils’ names or identifiable cases. Platform guidance is newly written and is not the original administration script.

questions.prompt: I explicitly present the learning objectives to the students at the beginning of the lesson/activity.
During the lesson/activity, I explain the purpose of each task I propose.
I check that the students understand the meaning and interest of the lessons/activities I propose.
I ask the students about their perception of the reasons why the lessons/activities are proposed.
Students know the purpose or objective of the lesson/activity in progress.
Students know why they are doing a particular activity.
Students understand why they are doing a specific task.
I modify goals and expectations for students with difficulties.
At the start of each lesson/activity, I give a brief summary/review of the previous lesson/activity.
I make links between the different activities I propose to the students.
I draw the students' attention to the main points of the lesson/activity.
At the end of the lesson/activity, I summarise what has been seen/worked on.
The students make links between the lesson/activity in progress and other previous lessons/activities.
Students are able to explain what happened in the previous lesson/activity.
At the end of the lesson/activity, the students summarise what they have seen/worked on.
I adjust the amount of work required in accordance with students' capabilities.
I plan different assignments to match students’ abilities.
I ask group oral questions (addressed to the whole class).
I ask individual oral questions (addressed specifically to certain students).
I ask written questions.
I ask open questions that require a developed/elaborated response.
The questions I ask are understood by the students.
Students respond correctly to the questions I ask them individually.
Students want to answer when I ask the class a collective question.
I explain strategies and procedures to students and then ask them to apply them.
If a student is having particular difficulty with an exercise, I show him/her the correct strategy or procedure to use.
To complete an exercise or solve a problem, I ask the students to use the strategies and procedures I have shown them.
When faced with an exercise or a problem, the students come up with their own strategies or procedures for solving it.
When faced with an exercise or problem situation, the students correctly apply the strategies and procedures I have shown them.
The students easily understand the strategies and procedures I explain to them.
I give written application exercises to be done individually.
I give you written exercises to do in pairs.
I give written exercises to be done in groups.
I give oral exercises to apply what has just been taught.
The exercises I give are specific (they target a particular skill or type of task).
The exercises I give involve the integration of several skills.
The exercises I give are corrected collectively in class or by myself during or after school.
I vary the complexity of assignments to match students’ abilities (e.g. make judgments about a text or summarize, recognize the main theme).
I make sure that every pupil participates in the lesson/activity.
I give positive feedback to the students.
The classroom atmosphere is calm and serene.
I encourage students to tell me when they don't understand something.
I use alternative materials to match students’ abilities (e.g. books adapted to the needs of lower and higher skill levels).
I provide weaker students with additional aids and tools (e.g. visual aids containing essential information).
My assessments are truly formative for the students.
I analyze the most common mistakes made during assessments in order to identify precisely what needs to be worked on as a priority with all or some of the students.
I observe the students while they are doing a particular task in class and give them direct feedback on their work.
After each assessment, I provide feedback to the students on which aspects they have mastered well and on which aspects they need to make further efforts.
After each assessment, I give additional explanations to students who are struggling.
After each assessment, I design remedial activities (set up a corrective procedure) for students in difficulty.
I adapt evaluations to match students’ abilities (by proposing different questions or by modulating my level of requirement).
I assess the progress of weak students.
I analyze data about students' academic progress.
I evaluate the effectiveness of teaching adjustments (e.g. monitor subsequent achievement and progress).
I use students’ data to make decisions about teaching adjustments.
